title: Model Catalog Demo - Medisys Solutions
next_steps: Send model compatibility matrix and benchmark spreadsheet
Share SOC 2 & compliance pack and VPC deployment notes
Schedule a 1-hour pilot planning call next week (Raj + Samir)
Estimate cost for 100k monthly tokens across top 3 candidate models
action_items: Raj Patel: Export perf benchmarks for Llama2, Mistral, and Redwood-verified models (due: 2026-05-04)
Lena Morris: Send pricing and Dedicated vs Hosted comparison doc (due: 2026-05-01)
Priya Desai: Provide list of required compliance artifacts for internal review (due: 2026-05-06)
summary: Quick walkthrough of Redwood's model catalog, focusing on selecting open models, interpreting benchmark results, and compatibility for VPC/private deployments. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for latency-sensitive triage use case; security/compliance and model quantization tradeoffs were top concerns.
topics: Next steps: benchmarks, pricing, pilot plan
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Morris: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood inference, i'll kick us off. uh, quick intro round.
[00:07] Taylor Nguyen: Hi, Taylor here, CTO at Medisys, Samir's on the call and Priya for security.
[00:12] Samir Khan: Hey, Samir, MLOps. thanks.
[00:15] Raj Patel: Raj here, technical solutions engineer. i'll do the demo and benchmarks slide.
[00:20] Lena Morris: Great. goal today is a short demo of the model catalog, how we pick open models, read benchmarks, and show compatibility for VPC and private installs. total 45 minutes, hope that works.
[00:31] Taylor Nguyen: yep good. main thing for us is latency SLO sub 200 ms for triage prompts and data residency in eu-west-1, also want cost estimates.
[00:42] Raj Patel: Understood. i'll show three candidate open models we usually recommend: Llama2 variants, Mistral 7B, and Red- uh Redwood-verified smaller models. We'll also show quantized runs, and the compatibility matrix for Dedicated and Private.
[00:55] Raj Patel: Jumping in, here's the model catalog page, you can filter by architecture, size, license. note the benchmarks card to the right shows tokens/sec, p95 latency, and also NVidia Ampere vs H100 numbers, though sometimes the names get garbled in the export.
[01:10] Priya Desai: when you say Redwood verified, is that internal testing or independent third-party?
[01:14] Raj Patel: it's our internal benchmark harness but we surface methodology and raw data in the benchmark spreadsheet; we run with representative prompts and you can reproduce locally.
[01:22] Aisha Roberts: do you have KV cache or prefix caching support? we have long patient histories up to 8k tokens.
[01:29] Raj Patel: yes, KV cache support on the runtime, and we have prefix caching and automatic k v cash reuse for hot prefixes to reduce cost. sometimes transcript shows K V cash which is silly.
[01:40] Lena Morris: quick note on modes: hosted gives fastest time-to-value, dedicated for predictable throughput, private for full control (VPC or on-prem).
[01:50] Taylor Nguyen: our security team will push for private but we'd like to see cost delta.
[01:54] Lena Morris: absolutely.
[01:56] Raj Patel: switching to benchmarks: here is Llama2-13B unquantized on A100 — p95 around 220ms on our bench with a 256 token context; quantized int8 gets that down to ~150ms and halves memory footprint. with H100 numbers we often see slightly better throughput but depends on kernel selection.
[02:16] Samir Khan: are those numbers for single-request latency or batched throughput?
[02:20] Raj Patel: these are single-request p95 numbers with our continuous batching disabled; for high throughput workloads you can enable batching which changes the tradeoff.
[02:28] Taylor Nguyen: can you show the compatibility matrix for on-prem? we have mix of RTX and older Ampere cards.
[02:33] Raj Patel: sure, here's the matrix — rows are model families, columns are hardware and OS kernels. note: older Ampere cards need specific kernels and sometimes half-precision is limited; quantization profiles differ per hardware.
[02:46] Priya Desai: what about encryption at rest and KMS integration?
[02:50] Raj Patel: we integrate with customer KMS and HSM for Private, and hosted supports our KMS overlay; we'll send the SOC2 and compliance pack.
[02:58] Lena Morris: for med records we usually recommend private or dedicated with bring-your-own-key if you need tenant-level control.
[03:06] Samir Khan: for model selection, we care about accuracy/perf tradeoff on triage prompts which are short but require medical terminologies. any model recommendation?
[03:15] Raj Patel: for short clinical triage, Mistral 7B often gives a surprising balance of latency and quality, Llama2-13B gives better accuracy on some benchsets but costs more; we can run your prompt set through our eval harness for a direct comparison.
[03:31] Taylor Nguyen: can you run against our prompt set? Samir will share it.
[03:34] Samir Khan: yes we'll upload a 200 prompt set, that's part of pilot.
[03:38] Raj Patel: perfect. next slide shows the model variant compatibility — GMP licenses, fine-tuned vs base. some models have restrictions for commercial use so we flag that.
[03:48] Aisha Roberts: what's the fallback if a dedicated pool gets overloaded?
[03:52] Raj Patel: smart routing — we can route to hosted or lower-cost variants as fallback; policies are configurable with automatic fallback.
[03:59] Priya Desai: logging and audit — are the logs tenant-separated and do you maintain token-level tracing?
[04:05] Lena Morris: yes per-route logs, token-level cost breakdown is available in Redwood Console; for private we can provide audit log exports.
[04:12] Samir Khan: how does quantization affect hallucinations or output quality? we worried about clinical correctness.
[04:18] Raj Patel: quantization (int8, int4) can affect model fidelity on edge cases. our Optimize toolkit suggests profiles by workload and flags quality regressions with evals. We recommend evaluating on your clinical prompt set.
[04:31] Taylor Nguyen: timeline — we're aiming to pilot inside 3 weeks and decide by end of Q2.
[04:35] Lena Morris: good. we'll align next steps after demo.
[04:38] Raj Patel: jumping into live Console demo — model catalog filters, bench details, and a compare view for selected models. here i'm toggling quantization to see latency changes.
[04:51] Raj Patel: you can see a compatibility badge: green for supported on Private with our runtime, yellow for partially supported (needs special kernel), red for unsupported.
[05:00] Priya Desai: are container images provided for private installs?
[05:03] Raj Patel: yes, we provide signed images, helm charts, and an installer for on-prem; for VPC we provide terraform modules to create the infra and guidance for subnet routing.
[05:13] Aisha Roberts: do you have a matrix of driver versions? our infra team is strict.
[05:17] Raj Patel: yes, full driver/kernel matrix and a recommended stack; i'll include in the artifacts.
[05:23] Samir Khan: about benchmarks reproducibility — can we run the benchmark harness in our environment?
[05:26] Raj Patel: you can, we open source portions of the harness and provide a reproducible container; for private installs we'll help run it.
[05:33] Taylor Nguyen: pricing question — if we use dedicated with reserved capacity, what does the pricing model look like?
[05:38] Lena Morris: reserved capacity is an annual/monthly commit with throughput SLAs; there's a base platform fee for private. i'll send a detailed sheet but quick estimate we'll run for 100k tokens/month across three models in next steps.
[05:50] Samir Khan: what about model updates and rollouts? how do you handle canarying?
[05:54] Raj Patel: Console supports rollouts, canary and A/B, automatic fallback by policy, plus tracing hooks to inspect regressions.
[06:02] Priya Desai: any third party audits for private installs?
[06:05] Lena Morris: we have SOC2 for hosted, and we provide artifacts and guidance for your own audits on private.
[06:11] Raj Patel: demo continued — here's the benchmark CSV download; i'll open the Llama2 vs Mistral sheet, note columns: prompt_id, avg_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_generated, failure_rate, and environment tags.
[06:26] Raj Patel: small transcription glitch: some proper names are odd in the export, so we recommend using the raw CSV for analysis.
[06:33] Samir Khan: what's failure_rate here? OOMs or timeouts?
[06:36] Raj Patel: it's both OOM and inference timeouts; we mark runs that exceed the SLO.
[06:41] Aisha Roberts: for long contexts 8k, any perf numbers?
[06:44] Raj Patel: yes, for 8k we see latency increases and memory growth; recommended to use KV cache and prefix sharding; some quant profiles help but you must test accuracy.
[06:57] Taylor Nguyen: can you show an example of the compatibility matrix entry for Mistral 7B on Ampere?
[07:02] Raj Patel: sure — Mistral 7B: supported on Ampere with int8 profiles, recommended kernels X and Y, container image tag v1.8, note that older drivers need manual kernel selection.
[07:17] Samir Khan: any gotchas with multi-tenant dedicated pools? we want strong isolation.
[07:22] Lena Morris: Dedicated offers tenant isolation and optional VPC peering; we also support per-tenant KMS.
[07:30] Priya Desai: do you keep any customer data? retention policies?
[07:34] Raj Patel: hosted does short-term logs by default with configurable retention, private you control retention.
[07:39] Taylor Nguyen: ok next, can you run our short prompt live? we have a sample.
[07:44] Raj Patel: sure go ahead and paste one.
[07:47] Samir Khan: (paste) "Patient with chest pain, troponin normal, shortness of breath, what next triage level?"
[07:55] Raj Patel: running against Mistral 7B quantized int8 on hosted bg node... result: "urgent evaluation recommended, suggest ED referral".
[08:08] Taylor Nguyen: that was fast. what's the p95 you saw?
[08:12] Raj Patel: live demo uses low-latency routing; p95 around 130ms in this environment.
[08:18] Aisha Roberts: any rate limiting or quotas?
[08:21] Lena Morris: yes per-account quotas, burst policies, and token-based rate limits, configurable in Console.
[08:28] Raj Patel: back to model choice — for high accuracy on medical terms we recommend evaluating on your labeled set; our Optimize will give recommendations (quantization, batching, caching) to meet latency/cost targets.
[08:40] Samir Khan: can Optimize give exact cost delta estimates for int8 vs fp16?
[08:44] Raj Patel: it gives delta estimates using historical workload characteristics; we'll provide a spreadsheet with expected cost per 1M tokens per model/quant profile.
[08:56] Taylor Nguyen: what about downstream hallucination monitoring?
[08:59] Raj Patel: we have quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets; you can set thresholds and get alerted on metric drift.
[09:10] Priya Desai: if we need more detailed architecture, who do we talk to?
[09:13] Lena Morris: i'll connect you with Solutions Architecture, and Raj will lead the pilot.
[09:18] Raj Patel: noted. i'll follow up with the benchmark CSV and compatibility matrix.
[09:22] Lena Morris: recap and next steps — Raj shares benchmarks and compatibility matrix; Lena sends pricing and compliance pack; Samir uploads prompt set; schedule a pilot planning call.
[09:33] Taylor Nguyen: sounds good. any other questions?
[09:36] Priya Desai: none from security for now.
[09:38] Samir Khan: none.
[09:40] Lena Morris: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email.
[09:44] (end)
